Guidance & outlook: The ϐirst question is: in earlier calls, we have guided for 100% PAT growth for both FY26 and FY27 but have delivered 59% PAT in FY26 due to the deferment of the Actis deal.
So, that was the issue and, apart from that, yes, for this year's particular guidance, we have given a guidance of a ~40% to 50% CAGR.
And, we are expecting 200 MWp more apart from this 238 MWp -200 MWp more in this ϐinancial year only, and for the next ϐinancial year , it's like 400 MWp for FY28 and 400 MWp for FY29.
Growth & demand: During the year, our consolidated revenue grew by nearly 84% to over INR 1,814 crore.
EBITDA grew by over 73% to ~INR 425 crore, and PAT increased by ~59% to ~INR 250 crore while maintaining the healthy double- digit proϐitability.
So, the order book-the unexecuted order book-is somewhere around INR 6,800 crores as of now.
Margins & costs: In parallel, project execution across part of the industry was affected by political and administrative transitions in certain states, which impacted approval timelines, project execution schedules, and consequently, the timing of revenue commissioning and margin realization during the year.
This number largely we have covered multiple times: ~INR 1,814 crore revenue, with a PAT of ~INR 250-plus crore, EPS of ~INR 124-plus per share, EBITDA of ~INR 425 crore.
I'm personally reasonably happy with this EBITDA in the given scenario, and a PAT margin of close to 14%.
Capex & expansion: Last year , when we won the battery tenders, we won by some odd 1,000 MWh capacity.
So, just to add, last year, we added 200 MWh approximately capacity under the C&I segment.
The capacity by 2030 is 1 million metric tons per annum-still the same.
Balance sheet & cash: We are having A rating CRISIL A rating at an A- or similar credit pro ϐile, leverage and borrowing costs are very different from AA and AAA -rated long-duration funds.
I don't think we have that leverage available, but still, you may check in the market what kind of tenders and projects are there.
So, deϐinitely, it will get better and leverage will get better.
Risks & challenges: Obviously, there are deϐinitely certain challenges -land challenges are there, connectivity challenges are there, ROW challenges are there.
We are building those positive things into the business, keeping ourselves isolated and protected from those riskier calls, riskier things, and keeping ourselves ready for the big rocket launch.

So, we are ready to accept the challenges, and we try to mitigate and ϐind solutions for those risks, build our strength, make ourselves more capable, and make more better strategies for all these kinds of challenges.

OUTLOOK The global economy is expected to gradually regain momentum over the medium term, with growth projected to average 2.8% in FY28 as energy supplies recover, inflation subsides, and monetary conditions ease.

Under current policy, combined biogas and CBG supply is projected to grow 53% between 2025 and 2030, while CBG production alone is expected to increase more than seven-fold, supported by mandatory blending obligations rising from 1% in FY26 to 5% by FY29 and expanding city gas infrastructure.
Growth & demand: Against that backdrop, we delivered revenue growth of ~84% to ₹1,813.67 crore, EBITDA growth of 73% to approximately ₹425 crore, and PAT growth of 59% to ₹252 crore - growth built on strengthening the foundations of a business designed to evolve with the changing architecture of energy itself.
The OECD projects India's GDP growth at 6.3% in FY27 and 6.4% in FY28, reflecting the impact of higher global energy prices, geopolitical uncertainties, and softer external demand.
In FY25, low-emissions sources, including solar, wind, nuclear, and hydropower, contributed nearly 60% of the growth in global energy demand.
